In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self stabilization is obtained when the velocity is taken into account, and self synchronization is obtained when the switching is based on the CoM position.

self synchronization can be achieved in both sagittal and frontal directions when the switching of the stance leg depends on the CoM position in both directions, and self stabilization can be achieved when the switching depends on the CoMs velocities in both sagittal plane and the frontal plane.

self synchronization and self stabilization of walking gaits can be obtained when both the step width and length vary, and when the switching of stance legs is based on a combination of the CoM positions in the sagittal and lateral directions, and on its velocity in the sagittal direction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
self synchronization can be achieved by using the position information, whereas self stabilization can be achieved by the velocity information of the CoM.
self synchronization and self stabilization can be achieved when the switching condition is based on the configuration of CoM. The simulation results show that
self synchronization and self stabilization are not always observed in walking gaits.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the switching condition of both the stance leg and the swing foot are important to achieve self synchronization and self stabilization of the walking gaits, and that a combination of both the position and velocity of the CoMs is necessary for self stabilization of the motion.
the switching conditions based on the position or velocity of the CoMs are more suitable than the ones based on time or fixed step length and width.
a simple switching condition based on the CoM position in the sagittal and in the frontal plane is enough to obtain self synchronization and self stabilization.
